title_as_printed: Experimental solubility of 2,2,4-trimethyl-pentane (iso-octane) in pure water (mole fraction), this work.

footnotes_as_printed.general: n = number of samples analyzed, x = mole fraction in aqueous phase, sigma_x = ((n x sum x^2 - (sum x)^2)/n x (n-1))^1/2.

pressure_note: P printed per row (about 0.5 MPa); paper does not say whether it is total pressure or what gas (a methane cylinder 'for pressurizing system' and pressurized nitrogen appear in the Fig. 1 legend) sets it; not stated

value.what: mole fraction of 2,2,4-trimethyl-pentane (iso-octane) in the aqueous phase, pure water (salt-free by construction)

uncertainty.what: two standard deviations of the n replicate samples

notes: 2,2,4-trimethyl-pentane (iso-octane) is a liquid hydrocarbon (not one of the seven standard gases); static-analytic method with Rolsi sampler. Whether a hydrocarbon-rich liquid phase is present is not stated explicitly, so regime left empty.
quality_remarks: Printed values kept: x at 313.15 K (3.45E-07) is below the 298.15 K value, and the 343.16 K row is at 0.440 MPa instead of about 0.5 MPa (confirmed on the page image). Possible misprints or real scatter; not changed.
